findings.text: The six refused-row panels still mark the reference admitted saddle with no contour through it, the second defect named by followup f-fsa-figrepair-shafranov ('no separatrix reaches the marked saddle'), left unaddressed while the node's manifest states the followup is addressed. In benchmarks/shafranov_pair_receipt.py the panel draws poloidal.contour_levels(reference_field, count=12) without naming the reference boundary flux, whereas the sibling state panels use state_contour_levels which replaces the nearest level with the boundary value so the separatrix is guaranteed among the drawn lines (nova/media/poloidal.py contour_levels boundary argument). A crop of row-21978-35.png shows the filled-cross saddle marker sitting in a region no contour line reaches, so a reader sees a marked X-point with no separatrix - the misleading marking the followup exists to remove. Repair: pass the reference topology's boundary flux (and axis flux) to contour_levels for the row panels, as the state panels already do, and add a test that the saddle's boundary flux is among the drawn levels.

The strip's suptitle is clipped off the right edge of its canvas, a legibility regression introduced by this commit in the same change that repairs clipped titles elsewhere. The base strip title ended '...the magnetics read three ways' and fit the 1296 px canvas; the new title '...the magnetics read two ways (the row kernel equals the circular reading, residual 0.0)' is passed un-wrapped to figure.suptitle and its last words run off the right edge (verified by cropping the top band of both the head and base PNGs). The node wrapped the fit figure's suptitle (textwrap width 118) but not the strip's, and no test measures any title extent, so this would pass the whole gate. Repair: wrap the strip suptitle the same way the fit suptitle is wrapped, and record the measured extent so a later title cannot overflow unnoticed.

justifications.durability: Each regenerated figure's receipt is refreshed with its new keys and sha256 together: the row panels record caption_lines, caption_widest_inches and canvas_width_inches beside a fresh figure sha256, and the strip receipt records series_policy beside fresh png/svg sha256, so a figure edited without its receipt, or a caption drifted from its source, fails the added tests. The vector twins now emit text (matplotlib svg.fonttype 'none') rather than glyph outlines, which is more durable for a reader and matches the plan's rule that vector figures carry text. The renders are redrawn from committed receipts and banked reference states through new render-only paths, so no equilibrium is solved and the figures are reproducible from the repository. Deducted for the strip suptitle: the node measures and records a caption extent for the row panels but records no extent for the strip suptitle, which it lengthened in the same commit and which overflows the canvas (finding 2); the title-legibility property is recorded where it was convenient and unmeasured where it regressed, and no test pins any title extent.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced first-hand. The head gate re-run in the reviewed worktree at 12a894f2 gives 44 passed, EXIT=0 (logs/review-gate-head.log), matching after_suite; the run printed the imported benchmark module as the worktree's path, so the worktree's code, not the main checkout behind the editable install, is what ran. The declared negative control was independently re-derived rather than trusted: the base-revision figures at 0dfce2a0d were reconstructed file-for-file with read-only 'git show' (38 files) into a scratch tree, and the head test file run against them gives 8 failed / 15 passed, EXIT=1 (logs/review-negctrl-repro.log) with failure ids that are exactly the reviewed run's: the six test_shafranov_row_panel_subtitle_fits_the_canvas parametrisations, test_combination_strip_does_not_advertise_the_covered_series and test_combination_strip_receipt_records_the_merged_series. So the guard is shown to fire on the exact defect it names. The added tests read the committed artifacts (receipt caption lines and measured extent, the strip receipt's series_policy, the fit receipt's arm verdict and the drawn SVG text), not a re-run of the driver. Deductions: (a) the strip suptitle regression in finding 2 is unguarded - no test measures any title's extent, so the very defect class (a title longer than its canvas) the node repaired for the fit figure survives on the strip and would pass every test; (b) the baseline arm's log base_gate.log records the summary line but no 'EXIT=' line, so the manifest's exit_status 0 for that arm rests on the summary rather than a recorded exit code.
justifications.fit: The change reuses the committed nova.media painters (poloidal.contour_levels, draw_flux_contours, draw_nulls, draw_wall) and adds render-only paths to the two existing benchmark drivers rather than new scripts, so a caption or series-policy repair costs a render rather than a solve; the merged-series policy is a clean way to stop advertising a series the discrete square hides, and the strip's moved series is recorded in the receipt rather than only in the drawing. The svg.fonttype 'none' context is a small, correct change applied to both the fit and the state SVG writers. Deducted for inconsistent title handling: the fit figure's suptitle and panel titles are wrapped (textwrap width 118 and 54), while the strip suptitle, lengthened in the same commit, is passed un-wrapped to figure.suptitle and overflows the 1296 px canvas - one legibility mechanism applied on one figure and not on the other in the same change.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Plan nova:constraint-augmented-newton-krylov section 4; the done-when names four items and directs the worker to read followup f-fsa-figrepair-shafranov, f-fsa-figrepair-shafranov-discriminator and f-fsa-figrepair-flux-function-fit in full and repair the remaining audited figures 'as the followups state'. (1) The six shafranov/ row panels' refusal subtitle is wrapped and now fits the canvas: verified in row-21978-35.png (four wrapped title lines inside the 4.8 in canvas) and receipt caption_widest_inches 2.5 < canvas_width_inches 4.8, pinned by test_shafranov_row_panel_subtitle_fits_the_canvas. (2) The combination strip no longer advertises the hidden magnetics (a) series the discrete square covered: verified in the strip PNG (four drawn series, legend labelling 'magnetics (a) == row kernel', the marker drawn once) and the receipt series_policy (drawn_series 4, merged_series [magnetics_circular, magnetics_discrete], residual max 0.0), pinned by test_combination_strip_does_not_advertise_the_covered_series and test_combination_strip_receipt_records_the_merged_series. (3) 'The remaining audited figures repaired as the followups state' is PARTIAL: followup f-fsa-figrepair-shafranov names two defects in the six refused-row panels - the clipped subtitle AND 'no separatrix reaches the marked saddle'. The subtitle is repaired; the separatrix is not. The reference panel still draws poloidal.contour_levels(reference_field, count=12) (benchmarks/shafranov_pair_receipt.py:311) without naming the reference boundary flux, unlike the state panels whose state_contour_levels guarantees the boundary flux among the levels, so the separatrix level is not among the drawn lines; a crop of the admitted-saddle region of row-21978-35.png shows the filled-cross saddle marker sitting in a region no contour reaches (finding 1). (4) The flux-function-fit panel draws the reference contours the followup asks for: the third panel is titled 'reference flux, line contours on its own levels' and no longer claims a terminal flux, pinned by test_flux_function_fit_draws_the_reference_contours and test_flux_function_fit_title_carries_each_arms_verdict. Deducted because item (3) leaves a defect the followup names, and the manifest's evidence_inputs asserts all three followups 'are addressed by this commit', which overstates it.
justifications.scope_discipline: The single commit 12a894f23 changes 35 paths, every one inside the granted fence: benchmarks/shafranov_pair_receipt.py, benchmarks/shafranov_combination_discriminator.py, tests/test_shafranov_discriminator_render.py, the three figure directories docs/figures/constraint-augmented-newton-krylov/{shafranov,shafranov-discriminator,flux-function-fit} and the node's own evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/constraint-augmented-newton-krylov/cank-shafranov-figure-remainder.html. No plan file, shared sprint/index state, or concurrent-node path is touched; the commit is not on origin/main (expected worker flow - the coordinator owns merge). The reviewed worktree is clean at its head and git status shows nothing outside .venv. The commit carries a conventional subject with an explanatory body, no AI trailer, and no plan or ticket identifier. The new render-only entry points (render_row_panels and the render paths in the two benchmark drivers) live inside the granted driver paths and are the repo's established render-from-receipt pattern. The two tests/test_shafranov_{pair_receipt,combination_discriminator}.py files were in scope but not changed, which is fine.
